title: The l-adic field is the localization of its integers at a uniformizer
statement: Let $E/\Ql$ be a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Then the inclusion $\mathcal O_E\subset E$ makes $E$ a localization of $\mathcal O_E$ at $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]: the induced ring map $\mathcal O_E[1/\varpi_E]\to E$, $x/\varpi_E^n\mapsto x\varpi_E^{-n}$, is an isomorphism. Consequently, for every $\mathcal O_E$-module $M$, $M\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_E[1/\varpi_E]\cong M\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ as $E$-modules. Here tensor products are tensor products of modules [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and the left-hand side has its $E$-module structure transported through the displayed ring isomorphism.

source.place: node def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, the identification Hom ⊗_{O_E} E of the rationalization (implicit: O_E[1/ϖ_E]=E)

proof.text: Put $R=\mathcal O_E$ and $\pi=\varpi_E$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $R$ is a subring of the field $E$ and a uniformizer is nonzero. Using the fractions and operations of [def-weil-ring-localization-away], define $\phi:R[1/\pi]\to E$ by $\phi(x/\pi^n)=x\pi^{-n}$. If $\pi^k(x\pi^m-y\pi^n)=0$, then cancellation in $E$ gives $x\pi^{-n}=y\pi^{-m}$, so this is well defined. The fraction addition and multiplication formulas show directly that $\phi$ preserves addition, multiplication, and $1$, and $\phi(x/1)=x$. Conversely, equality of the two images implies $x\pi^m-y\pi^n=0$ in $R$, so the fractions are equal (take $k=0$). Thus $\phi$ is an injective $R$-algebra homomorphism.

proof.text: For $z=0$, $z=\phi(0/1)$. For $z\ne0$, clause 5 of [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] gives $z=u\pi^m$, where $u\in R^\times$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$. If $m\ge0$, then $u\pi^m\in R$ and $z=\phi((u\pi^m)/1)$. If $m=-n<0$, with $n\ge1$, then $z=\phi(u/\pi^n)$. This proves surjectivity. Together with Step 1 it gives the claimed ring isomorphism, and hence the localization assertion in [def-weil-ring-localization-away].

proof.text: Let $M$ be any $R$-module. Write $\psi=\phi^{-1}$. The bilinear universal property and generation by pure tensors in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] give maps $F(m\otimes t)=m\otimes\phi(t)$ and $G(m\otimes e)=m\otimes\psi(e)$. They respect the balancing relations because $\phi$ and $\psi$ fix $R$. Both composites fix every pure tensor, so they are identity maps. Transport the $E$-action on $M\otimes_R R[1/\pi]$ by $e(m\otimes t)=m\otimes\psi(e)t$. Then $F(e(m\otimes t))=m\otimes e\phi(t)=eF(m\otimes t)$; generation by pure tensors proves $E$-linearity. This proves the final clause without a flatness or finiteness hypothesis on $M$.
